finding: The live range of $90-$750 is about right, but it is wide because it joins two different jobs: a cleaning (roughly $70-$230) and a replacement (roughly $140-$705 on the vehicles checked). Showing them as two ranges would be clearer. Built replacement totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2020 Jeep Compass 2.4L, $246.99-$545.00 + 0.6-1.0 hr = about $319-$705; midsize 2018 Chevrolet Malibu 1.5L, $114.40-$233.38 + 0.2-0.8 hr = about $138-$361; truck 2016 Ford F-150 5.0L, $139.49-$400.73 + 0.5-1.0 hr = about $199-$561; luxury 2011 Cadillac CTS 3.6L, $228.99-$389.36 + 0.6-0.8 hr = about $288-$517. Two cautions on the low ends: the Malibu low is the genuine GM part at an online discount price, not an aftermarket part (none could be priced), and the F-150 low is a budget-brand aftermarket unit; with a name-brand or dealer part and a normal shop time, most replacements land between about $300 and $700. The truck example was moved from the 2018 to the 2016 F-150 5.0L because no aftermarket unit could be found for the 2018 part; the 2018-2020 genuine part lists at $545.82, so that truck builds to about $706 at the top. Cleaning only: a mechanic-written consumer guide (Jerry) gives 0.5-0.8 hr for a typical cleaning and 0.8-1.2 hr when the throttle body is removed for a deep clean, which is $60-$192 of labor at $120-$160/hr, plus about $10-$40 for cleaner and a gasket: roughly $70-$230. A relearn with a scan tool adds 0.2-0.4 hr ($24-$64) per the same guide; an Acura bulletin prints 0.2 hr for 'Reset the throttle position value and idle learn procedure'. One GM bulletin allows 1.2 hr for remove, clean, replace the sensor cover, relearn and diagnosis together. So the $90 floor fits a cleaning (lowest benchmark $90), and nothing found supports a replacement that cheap except the Malibu built on a discounted part and a 0.2 hr warranty time. The $750 top fits the mainstream cases but can be exceeded: RepairPal's average is $623-$766, YourMechanic shows $807-$1,204 at a shop or dealer for a 2017 F-150 3.5L turbo, and a 2024-2025 Jeep Wrangler 2.0L turbo bulletin allows 2.7 hr for the throttle body alone ($324-$432 of labor before parts). How solid the labor times are: every class has a manufacturer-stated time for the example vehicle (Compass 0.6 hr, Malibu 0.2 hr, 2016 F-150 0.5 hr, CTS 0.8 hr), but these are warranty times, the low end of what shops bill; the Malibu's 0.2 hr sits beside charge-air-tube work and looks optimistic as a stand-alone job, and the 2016 F-150 bulletin does not name the engine (a second Ford bulletin gives the same 0.5 hr for the 2018 5.0L). The other ends are not for the example vehicles: an older-Malibu GM time, a Lincoln time, and a general 50-60 minute figure from a consumer guide; a parts seller's do-it-yourself estimate of about 2 hours for an older F-150 5.0L suggests the 1.0 hr top can be exceeded. Half of the eight hour figures are not for the example vehicle, which is why confidence stays low. Parts: every class now has two priced sources, but the luxury example is an older domestic car; no European luxury throttle body was priced, and those can cost more. Our totals sit below RepairPal mainly because its parts figure ($492-$573) is higher than the list prices found for the Malibu, the 2016 F-150 and the CTS. An estimate is never a quote and never a diagnosis. Reviewer note: the luxury low is the genuine GM part at a discount retailer ($216.09), giving about $288-$517; the Dorman price is kept only as a cross-check because its page prints the price without a decimal point.
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis or scan fee, a new throttle body gasket (about $18 list on the Compass), shop supplies and tax. Many shops try a cleaning first: about 0.5-1.2 hr of labor plus cleaner, roughly $70-$230. After either a cleaning or a replacement, most drive-by-wire cars need an idle/throttle relearn, which some shops include and others bill at about 0.2-0.4 hr. An air filter, intake tube or clamp, or a wiring connector repair may be quoted at the same time. An estimate is not a quote and not a diagnosis: the same warning light or reduced-power message can come from wiring, the pedal sensor or a vacuum leak.
